1.word_for_word: त्रयोदशे — in the thirteenth chapter; अहरत् ब्रह्मा वत्सान् पालांश् च मायया — Brahmā stole the calves and their keepers by māyā; तदा तत्-सर्व-रूपः कृष्णः — then Kṛṣṇa assumed all their forms; अब्दं पूर्ववत् आचरत् — for a year He behaved just as before; नूतनयसि — you make it new; नव्यवत् करोषि — you present it as fresh.
1.translation: In the thirteenth chapter Brahmā, by his māyā, stole the calves and their keepers. Kṛṣṇa then became the forms of all of them and for a full year acted exactly as they had before. ‘You make it new’ means that the narration presents the event as ever fresh.

2.word_for_word: सार-भृतां सार-ग्रहिणाम् — of those who grasp the essence; अयं निसर्गः स्वभावः — this is their natural disposition; अच्युतस्य वार्ता श्रुता सती — a narration of Acyuta, once heard; प्रतिक्षणं साधु नव्यवत् भवति — becomes beautifully new at every moment; विटानां स्त्रैणानां स्त्रियाः कामिन्या वार्ता इव — like talk of a beloved woman to sensual men; या अच्युत-वार्ता सा एव अर्थः येषां वाणी-श्रुति-चेतांसि — for those whose speech, hearing and mind have Acyuta’s narration as their sole object.
2.translation: This is the natural disposition of those who grasp the essence: a narration concerning Acyuta, though already heard, becomes beautifully new at every moment. It is like talk of a beloved woman to sensual men, but here even the speech, hearing and mind of the saints have the narration of Acyuta alone as their object.

5.word_for_word: भोजन-विधानाय पुलिनं स्तौति — for arranging the meal he praises the riverbank; स्वीयानां केलीनां संपदः विद्यन्ते यस्मिन् — a place possessing all resources for their play; मृदुला-अच्छा-वालुका — with soft, clean sand; स्फुटत् विकसत् सरः — a lake blooming openly; सरोज-बाहुल्येन उपचारतः सरः एव विकसत् — because of the profusion of lotuses, the lake itself is figuratively said to bloom; तस्य गन्धेन हृताः अलयः पत्रिणश् च — bees and birds drawn by its fragrance; उदके ध्वनयः प्रतिध्वानाः — echoes of their sounds over the water; तैर् लसन्तः द्रुमाः — trees made lively by those echoes.
5.translation: To describe the place chosen for the meal, he praises the riverbank: it possessed everything suited to their games and had soft, clean sand. The lake was said to ‘blossom’ because of its abundance of lotuses. Bees and birds were drawn by their fragrance, and the trees seemed alive with the echoes of their sounds across the water.

6.word_for_word: दिवा रूढम् — the day had advanced; वेला अतीता — the proper mealtime had passed.
6.translation: The day had advanced; that is, the usual mealtime had already passed.

7.word_for_word: आरुध्य — enclosing, surrounding; संरुध्य — restraining within; शाद्वले — on grassy ground; हरित-तृणे देशे — in a place covered with green grass.
7.translation: ‘Śādvale’ means on a place covered with fresh green grass; the calves were gathered and kept there.

8.word_for_word: कृष्णस्य विष्वक् परितः — all around Kṛṣṇa; पुरु-राजि-मण्डलैः — in many circular rows; नैरन्तर्येण उपविष्टाः — seated closely without gaps; श्री-कृष्ण-अभिमुखानि आननानि — with faces turned toward Śrī Kṛṣṇa; फुल्ल-दृशः — with blossoming, wide-open eyes; कमल-कर्णिकायाः परितः पत्राणि यथा — like petals around a lotus pericarp.
8.translation: They shone as they sat close together in many circular rows all around Kṛṣṇa, every face turned toward Him and every eye opened wide with delight, like lotus petals arranged around the central pericarp.

9.word_for_word: पुष्पैः तद्-दलैः — with flowers and their petals; अन्यैः च पत्रैः — and with other leaves; कृतानि भाजनानि यैः ते — those who made their eating vessels from them.
9.translation: They made their plates and bowls from flowers, flower-petals, leaves and other natural materials.

10.word_for_word: रुचिम् — relish; स्वाद-विशेषम् — a particular taste; अभ्यवजह्रुः — they ate; बुभुजिरे — they partook; सह-ईश्वराः — together with their Lord; श्री-कृष्ण-सहिताः — together with Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
10.translation: ‘Ruci’ means a distinctive relish or taste. The boys ate their food together with their Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

11.word_for_word: यज्ञ-भुक् अपि तेषु बुभुजे — though He is the enjoyer of sacrifice, He ate among them; बालानाम् इव केलिः यस्य — His play was like that of an ordinary child; उदर-वस्त्रयोर् मध्ये वेणुं बिभ्रत् — carrying the flute between belly and cloth; वाम इति कक्ष-पाण्योः विशेषणम् — ‘left’ qualifies both armpit and hand; मसृणं स्निग्धं दध्योदन-कवलम् — a soft, moist morsel of rice mixed with yogurt; बिल्वामलकादि-फलानि अङ्गुलि-सन्धिषु — bilva, āmalaka and similar fruits placed between His fingers; कर्णिका इव सर्वाभिमुखः मध्ये तिष्ठन् — standing in the middle facing all, like a lotus pericarp; स्वैर् नर्मभिः परिहास-वाक्यैः — with His own joking words; स्वर्गे जने आश्चर्येण पश्यति सति — while the inhabitants of heaven watched in amazement.
11.translation: Although He is the enjoyer of all sacrifices, Kṛṣṇa ate among the boys and played like one of them. His flute was tucked between His belly and garment; ‘left’ qualifies both His armpit and hand. He held a soft morsel of yogurt-rice and tucked bilva, āmalaka and other fruits between His fingers. Standing in the center like the pericarp of a lotus and facing all His friends, He delighted them with jokes while the inhabitants of heaven watched in astonishment.

13.word_for_word: भी-भयम् — fear itself; भय-हेतुभ्यः भयम् अस्य अपास्य — removing fear arising from causes of fear; यद् वा — alternatively; अस्य विश्वस्य भियः अपि भयम् यः श्री-कृष्णः — Śrī Kṛṣṇa is the very fear of the fear of this universe; आशात् — from eating; भोजनात् — from the meal; अक्षराधिक्यम् आर्षम् — the extra syllable is an archaic/ṛṣi usage.
13.translation: The expression may mean that Kṛṣṇa removes the boys’ fear of every source of danger; alternatively, He is Himself the fear of whatever frightens the entire universe. ‘Āśāt’ means ‘from eating, from the meal.’ The metrical excess of a syllable is an archaic usage of the seers.

14.word_for_word: अद्रिषु तेषां दरीषु — in the caves of those mountains; कुञ्जेषु — in bowers; लतादि-पिहित-उदर-विवरेषु — in hollow interiors concealed by creepers and the like; गह्वरेषु च — and in caverns.
14.translation: They searched in mountain caves, in bowers whose inner hollows were concealed by creepers and similar growth, and in other caverns.

15.word_for_word: अम्भो-जन्मनः पद्मात् जनिः यस्य सः ब्रह्मा — Brahmā, whose birth was from the lotus born of the waters; तद्-अनन्तरे तस्मिन् अवसरे आगतः — who arrived at that moment; तच्-छिद्रं प्राप्तः वा — or who found that opportunity; मञ्जु मनोहरम् अन्यद् अपि महित्वं द्रष्टुम् — to see another charming manifestation of Kṛṣṇa’s greatness; वत्सान् इतः पुलिनात् — the calves from this riverbank; वत्सपांश् च अन्यत्र नीत्वा — and then the calf-herd boys, taking them elsewhere; स्वयं तिरोबभूव — he himself disappeared; प्रभवतः श्री-कृष्णस्य — of the all-powerful Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
15.translation: Brahmā, born from the lotus that arose from the cosmic waters, came at that moment—or found that opening—in order to witness another charming display of all-powerful Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s greatness. He carried the calves away from the riverbank and then took the calf-herd boys elsewhere as well, after which he himself disappeared.

16.word_for_word: उभौ अपि — both groups; वत्सान् वत्सपांश् च — the calves and their keepers; विचिकाय — He searched for; अन्वीक्षितवान् — He looked about for them.
16.translation: ‘Both’ means both the calves and the calf-herd boys. Kṛṣṇa searched and looked about for them.

17.word_for_word: विधि-कृतम् — done by Vidhi; ब्रह्मणा कृतम् — done by Brahmā.
17.translation: ‘Done by Vidhi’ means that it had been done by Brahmā.

18.word_for_word: उभयायितम् — becoming both; वत्स-तत्-पाल-रूपेण वर्तमानम् — existing in the forms of the calves and their keepers; यदि तूष्णीम् आसे — if I remain silent and do nothing; तन्-मातॄणां विषादः स्यात् — their mothers will be distressed; यदि तान् एव आनयिष्यामि — if I simply bring the originals back; ब्रह्मणः मोहः न स्यात् — Brahmā will not be bewildered; तद्-उभय-प्रीतये तथा चक्रे — for the satisfaction of both sides He acted in this way.
18.translation: ‘Becoming both’ means that Kṛṣṇa Himself became the calves and their keepers. His thought was: ‘If I do nothing, their mothers will grieve; if I merely bring the originals back, Brahmā will not be bewildered.’ To satisfy both purposes, He therefore became all of them Himself.

19.word_for_word: वत्सपानां वत्सकानां च अल्पकं वपुः — the small bodies of the calf-herd boys and calves; यत्-प्रमाणकं न अनतिक्रम्य — without exceeding the exact measure of each; दलम् — a leaf-shaped musical instrument; यद् वा वेणु-दलम् — or a piece of bamboo; शिक् — a carrying-sling; यावत् वत्सपादि-वपुः तावत् सर्व-स्वरूप-अजः कृष्णः बभौ — to the full extent of every calf and boy’s body, unborn Kṛṣṇa appeared as all their forms; ‘सर्वं विष्णु-मयं जगत्’ — ‘the whole universe is pervaded by Viṣṇu’; स्वरूपेण प्रत्यक्षा यथा तथा बभौ — that statement became directly visible in embodied form.
19.translation: Kṛṣṇa reproduced the small body of every calf and every boy without exceeding its exact measure, together with each flute, leaf-instrument, sling and other possession. Thus the unborn Lord appeared as the complete form of every calf and calf-herd boy. The familiar declaration ‘the whole universe is pervaded by Viṣṇu’ became, as it were, directly visible in His very forms.

20.word_for_word: सर्वात्मा सन् व्रजं प्राविशत् — being the Self of all, He entered Vraja; स्वयम् आत्मा इव प्रयोजकः — He Himself was the directing agent; आत्म-रूपान् गो-वत्सान् — the calves were His own forms; आत्म-रूपैः वत्स-पैः प्रतिवार्य — driven along by calf-herds who were also His own forms; प्रयोज्य-कर्ता अपि स्वयम् एव — He Himself was also the acting agent; आत्म-विहारैः क्रीडन् — playing through pastimes that were Himself; क्रिया अपि कारकाणि अपि स्वयम् एव — both action and all agents of action were He Himself.
20.translation: As the Self of all, Kṛṣṇa entered Vraja. He Himself was the director, the calves He drove were His own forms, the calf-herd boys who drove them were His own forms, and He Himself was the acting agent. Thus in this play both the action and every participant in the action were Kṛṣṇa Himself.

21.word_for_word: तत्-तद्-आत्मा — the self/form of each one; तत्-तद्-गोप-बाल-रूपः अभवत् — He became the form of each individual cowherd boy; ततः तत्-तत्-सद्म प्रविष्टः — then each such form entered its respective home.
21.translation: Kṛṣṇa became the individual form of every cowherd boy, and each of those forms then entered that boy’s own home.

22.word_for_word: गोपिका-मोहम् आह — he describes the enchantment of the cowherd mothers; तन्-मातरः वेणु-रवेण त्वरया उत्थिताः — their mothers hurriedly rose at the sound of the flute; सुतान् मत्वा परं ब्रह्म इव दोर्भिः उत्थाप्य — taking them for their sons, they lifted the Supreme Brahman in their arms; पयः-सुधा-आसवम् — milk that was sweet as nectar and intoxicating as wine; पाययाम् आसुः — they gave Him to drink.
22.translation: He now describes the enchantment of the cowherd mothers. Hearing the flute, they rose in haste and, believing the returning forms to be their own sons, lifted the Supreme Brahman in their arms. They gave Him their breast-milk, which was sweet like nectar and intoxicating like wine.

23.word_for_word: याम-यमेन — at each period of the day; तत्-तत्-काल-क्रीडा-नियमेन — according to the regular play proper to each time; सायं गतः — coming home in the evening; स्व-आचरितैः — by His own conduct, or by good behavior; मातॄः प्रहर्षयन् — delighting the mothers; उन्मर्दनादिभिः उपलालितः — cherished by them with massage and other attentions.
23.translation: At each period of the day He followed the customary play proper to that time. Returning in the evening, He delighted each mother by the behavior of her apparent son and was fondled by her with massage and other acts of care.

24.word_for_word: गवां मोहनम् आह — he describes the enchantment of the cows; परिहूताः — called back; आहूताः च ते सङ्गताः च तान् — the calves who had been summoned and gathered together.
24.translation: He next describes the enchantment of the cows. The calves were called back, summoned, and gathered together before them.

25.word_for_word: एतावत् तु वैषम्यं कृष्णस्य अपि दुर्निवारम् आसीत् — this one difference was difficult even for Kṛṣṇa to conceal; गवां गोपीनां च अस्मिन् कृष्णे मातृता पुरोवत् एव आसीत् — the maternal relation of cows and gopīs toward Kṛṣṇa remained as before; किन्तु स्नेह-ऋद्धिकां विना — except for an increase of affection; स्नेहाधिक्यं तु इदानीं विशेषः — the special feature now was greater love; हरेः तोकता बाल-भावना पूर्ववत् — Hari’s sense of being their child remained as before; किन्तु मायया विना — but without delusion; ‘ममेयं माता अहम् अस्याः पुत्रः’ इति मोहं विना — without the false notion ‘this is literally my mother and I am literally her son.’
25.translation: There was one difference that even Kṛṣṇa did not suppress. The cows and cowherd women related to Him maternally just as before, but their affection had now become far more intense. Kṛṣṇa likewise continued to behave as their child, yet without being deluded by the thought, ‘This is really my mother and I am her ordinary son.’

26.word_for_word: स्नेह-ऋद्धिम् एव दर्शयति — he specifically shows the growth of affection; यथा कृष्णे यशोदा-नन्दने स्व-पुत्रेभ्यः अपि स्नेहाधिक्यम् पूर्वम् आसीत् — formerly the people of Vraja loved Yaśodā’s son Kṛṣṇa even more than their own children; इदानीं स्व-तोकेषु अपि तथैव अवर्धत — now the same love increased toward their own apparent children; आ अब्दम् — up to a year; यावत् संवत्सरम् — throughout the year; निःसीम — without limit.
26.translation: Formerly the residents of Vraja had loved Yaśodā’s son Kṛṣṇa even more than their own children. Now, because those children were Kṛṣṇa Himself, that same extraordinary love increased toward their own apparent sons. It continued without limit throughout the entire year.

27.word_for_word: आत्मा श्री-कृष्णः वत्सपः भूत्वा — Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself became the calf-herd boys; वत्सानां पालानां च मिषेण — under the appearance of the calves and their keepers; आत्मानम् आत्मना पालयन् — protecting Himself by Himself; क्रीडितवान् — He played.
27.translation: Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself became the calf-herd boys and, under the appearances of both calves and keepers, protected Himself by Himself and continued His play.

28.word_for_word: एतावत्-पर्यन्तं रामस्य अपि मोहः एव आसीत् — until this point even Balarāma remained bewildered; संवत्सरान्ते तु कथञ्चित् ज्ञातवान् — at the end of the year he somehow understood; पञ्च-षासु — in five or six; रात्रिषु हायनस्य अपूरणीषु — when only five or six nights remained to complete the year.
28.translation: Until this point even Balarāma remained under the enchantment. Only at the end of the year did He begin to understand—when merely five or six nights remained before the year was complete.

29.word_for_word: दूरतः एव — from far away; गोवर्धन-शिखरे चरन्त्यः गावः — the cows grazing on the summit of Govardhana; व्रज-समीपे चरतः वत्सान् ददृशुः — saw the calves grazing near Vraja.
29.translation: From far away, the cows grazing high on Govardhana saw the calves grazing near Vraja below.

30.word_for_word: स गो-व्रजः गवां कलापः — that whole herd of cows; तत्-स्नेह-वशः — overcome by affection for the calves; वत्सानां स्नेहेन आकृष्टः — drawn by love for them; न स्मृत आत्मा येन — forgetting themselves; जवेन उपव्रजम् अगात् — rushed swiftly toward Vraja; अत्यात्म-पः — having passed beyond their cowherd protectors; दुर्गमः मार्गः यस्य — despite the difficult path; परस्पर-युक्ताभ्यां पध्यां धावन् द्वि-पाद् इव — running with paired legs so closely that they seemed two-legged; ककुदि आकुञ्चिता ग्रीवा — necks bent over their humps; उदास्य-पुच्छः — heads and tails raised; आस्रु-पयाः — milk streaming from every side; गो-व्रज इत्य् अनेन वृषभादयः अपि अगुः — ‘the cattle-herd’ includes bulls and the others as well.
30.translation: The entire herd was overcome by affection and drawn irresistibly toward the calves. Forgetting themselves, they rushed down toward Vraja, breaking past their cowherd protectors despite the difficult path. Their legs moved in paired unison so that they seemed almost two-footed; their necks bent over their humps, heads and tails were raised, and milk streamed from them. The expression ‘herd of cattle’ includes the bulls and the other animals as well.

31.word_for_word: धेनूनां चेष्टितम् आह — he particularly describes the cows’ behavior; गोवर्धनस्य अधः — at the foot of Govardhana; वत्सवत्यः पुनः प्रसूताः अपि — although they already had newly born calves of their own.
31.translation: He now specifies the cows’ behavior at the foot of Govardhana: even cows that had recently given birth to new calves of their own ran to the older calves below.

32.word_for_word: रामेण दृष्टं वत्सेषु गवां स्नेहातिशयम् उक्त्वा — having described the cows’ extraordinary affection for the calves as seen by Balarāma; गोपानाम् अपि दर्शयितुम् — to show the cowherds’ affection as well; गवां रोधने य आयासः तस्य मौघ्येन — ashamed that their effort to restrain the cows had been futile; सह उरु-मन्युना — together with great anger; दुर्ग-मार्ग-जनित-क्लेशेन — and exhaustion from the difficult route; अभ्येत्य — coming near; गोवत्सैः सह सुतान् ददृशुः — they saw their sons together with the calves.
32.translation: After describing to Balarāma the cows’ extraordinary love for the calves, Śuka shows the same phenomenon in the cowherds. Ashamed that their strenuous attempt to restrain the cows had failed, angry, and exhausted by the difficult descent, they approached and saw their sons standing with the calves.

33.word_for_word: तेषाम् ईक्षणेन उद्गतः प्रेम-रसः — the flood of love that arose on seeing their sons; तस्मिन् आप्लुताः निमग्नाः आशयाः — their hearts were submerged in it; ताडयितुम् आगताः सन्तः अपि — although they had come intending to chastise them; गत-मन्यवः — their anger vanished; प्रत्युत जातः अनुरागः — instead affection arose; मूर्धनि घ्राणैः अवघ्राणैः — by repeatedly smelling their heads; परमां मुदम् अवापुः — they obtained supreme joy.
33.translation: The moment they saw their sons, a flood of love arose and their hearts were submerged in it. Although they had come intending to chastise them, their anger disappeared and was replaced by intense affection. They repeatedly smelled the boys’ heads and attained the highest joy.

34.word_for_word: कृच्छ्रात् ततः अपगताः — with difficulty they departed from there; तेषां सुतानाम् अनुस्मृत्या — by remembering their sons; उद्गच्छन्ति अश्रूणि येषां ते — tears continued to rise in their eyes.
34.translation: Only with difficulty did the fathers tear themselves away. As they went, remembrance of their sons repeatedly brought tears to their eyes.

35.word_for_word: प्रेम-ऋद्धेः औत्कण्ठ्यम् अतिशयम् — the extraordinary intensity produced by the growth of love; मुक्त-स्तनेषु अपत्येषु — toward children already weaned from the breast; वीक्ष्य — seeing it; हेतुम् अजानन् — not knowing the cause; अचिन्तयत् — Balarāma reflected.
35.translation: Seeing this extraordinary increase of yearning and affection even toward children long since weaned, Balarāma could not understand its cause and began to reflect.

36.word_for_word: वासुदेवे यथा पुरा प्रेम — the love formerly directed toward Vāsudeva; तथा स्व-तोकेषु अपि व्रजस्य अपूर्वं प्रेम वर्धते — that same unprecedented love of Vraja is now increasing toward their own children; किम् एतद् अद्भुतम् — what is this marvel?; सात्मनः मत्-सहितस्य व्रजस्य — of Vraja together with myself; मम अपि एतेषु प्रेमातिशयः — even I feel extraordinary love for them; तत्र कारणं किम् — what is its cause?.
36.translation: Balarāma wondered: ‘The unprecedented love that Vraja formerly bore toward Vāsudeva’s Kṛṣṇa is now increasing in precisely the same way toward their own children. What is this wonder? Indeed, not only Vraja but I myself feel extraordinary affection for them. What is the cause?’

37.word_for_word: का इयं माया — whose māyā is this?; देवानां वा नराणां वा असुराणाम् — of gods, humans, or asuras?; कुतः वा कस्मात् प्रयुक्ता — from where, and by whom, has it been applied?; अन्य-माया न सम्भवति — no one else’s māyā can account for it; यतः मम अपि मोहः वर्तते — because even I am bewildered; प्रायशः मत्-स्वामिनः श्री-कृष्णस्य एव माया — therefore it is probably the māyā of my Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa Himself.
37.translation: He considered: ‘Whose māyā is this—of gods, humans, or asuras? From where and by whom has it been deployed?’ No ordinary māyā could explain it, because even Balarāma Himself was bewildered. He therefore concluded that it must most likely be the māyā of His own Lord, Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

38.word_for_word: स-वयसान् सखीन् अपि — even His friends of the same age; वयुनेन ज्ञान-मयेन चक्षुषा — with the eye consisting of knowledge; वैकुण्ठं श्री-कृष्णम् एव अपश्यत् — He saw them as none other than transcendent Śrī Kṛṣṇa.
38.translation: With the eye of spiritual knowledge Balarāma looked upon the boys, even His own companions of the same age, and saw that they were all none other than transcendent Śrī Kṛṣṇa.

39.word_for_word: कृष्ण-रूपान् सामान्यतः ज्ञात्वा — first understanding generally that they were forms of Kṛṣṇa; कृष्णं पृष्ट्वा कृष्णोपदेशेन विशेषतः ज्ञातवान् — then asking Kṛṣṇa and learning the details from His instruction; पाल्यमानाः वत्साः ऋषीणाम् अंशाः — I know that the original calves were portions of sages; पालाः च देवानाम् अंशाः — and the keepers portions of gods; इदानीं तु न तथा — but now it is not so; अस्मिन् भिद्-आश्रये अपि त्वम् एव भासि — even within this appearance of multiplicity, You alone shine; त्वं सर्वं पृथक् विविच्य कथं वृत्तम् इति वद — explain distinctly how all this occurred; प्रभुणा वक्त्रा निगमात् सङ्क्षेपतः उक्तम् — the Lord then briefly told Him the conclusion; वृत्तं बलः अवैद् — Balarāma understood what had happened.
39.translation: Balarāma first understood in a general way that all the boys and calves were forms of Kṛṣṇa. He then asked Kṛṣṇa and learned the details from Him: ‘I know that ordinarily these calves are portions of sages and the boys portions of gods, but that is not what I see now. Even in this apparent multiplicity You alone are shining. Please distinguish everything and tell me how this occurred.’ The Lord briefly explained the matter, and Balarāma understood the event.

40.word_for_word: वर्षे जाते — when a year had elapsed; आत्मनो मानेन त्रुटि-अनेहसा — by Brahmā’s own measure, in a time no longer than a truṭi; त्रुटि-मात्रेण कालेन — in merely an instant; स-कलं सानुचरं हरिं ददर्श — he saw Hari together with all His attendants.
40.translation: When an entire earthly year had passed—although by Brahmā’s own measure it was only the briefest instant, a truṭi—Brahmā returned and saw Hari together with all His companions.

41.word_for_word: दृष्ट्वा च व्यतर्कयत् — seeing them, he began to reason; मे मायाशये — in the resting-place of my māyā; मत्-माया-तल्पे — on the bed of my own māyā.
41.translation: Seeing the boys and calves there, Brahmā began to reason about what he was witnessing. The phrase refers to those whom he had placed within the resting-place, as it were the bed, of his own māyā.

42.word_for_word: मत्-माया-मोहितेभ्यः इतरे — these others, distinct from those bewildered by my māyā; कुत्रत्याः — where have they come from?.
42.translation: Brahmā wondered: ‘If the originals are those whom I bewildered with my māyā, where have these other boys and calves come from?’

43.word_for_word: इति वितर्कयन् अमुह्यत् — reasoning in this way, he himself became bewildered; एवम् एतेषु भेदेषु चिरं ध्यात्वा — contemplating these apparent differences for a long time; स आत्म-भूः इति पाठः — the reading is ‘sa ātma-bhūḥ,’ ‘that self-born Brahmā.’
43.translation: As Brahmā reasoned in this way, he himself became bewildered. He continued for a long time contemplating the apparent differences among the two sets. The reading is ‘sa ātma-bhūḥ,’ ‘that self-born Brahmā.’

45.word_for_word: मायाश्रयस्य तस्य कुतः मोहः — how could Brahmā, himself a wielder of māyā, be bewildered?; महा-मायाविनि भगवति अन्य-मायाया आवरण-विक्षेपकत्व-अभावे — another’s māyā cannot veil or project over Bhagavān, the supreme master of māyā; तम्यां रात्र्यां नैहारं तम इव — like darkness produced by mist within the darkness of night; तत् तमः पृथक् आवरणं न करोति किन्तु तत्र एव लीयते — such darkness makes no separate covering but dissolves into the greater darkness; खद्योत-अर्चिः अहनि पृथक् प्रकाशं न करोति — a firefly’s light gives no separate illumination in daylight; महति पुरुषे मायां युञ्जतः पुंसः इतरा नीचा माया — the lesser māyā of one who tries to apply it to the Supreme Person; तत्र न किञ्चित् करोति — can do nothing to Him; आत्मनि स्वस्मिन् एव ऐश्यं सामर्थ्यं निहन्ति — it only destroys or frustrates its wielder’s own power.
45.translation: One may ask how Brahmā, himself a wielder of māyā, could be bewildered. Śrīdhara answers that another’s māyā cannot veil or project anything over Bhagavān, the supreme master of māyā. Mist-born darkness has no separate effect in the darkness of night but disappears into it, and a firefly’s light produces no independent illumination in full daylight. In the same way, the inferior māyā of one who tries to use it against the Supreme Person does nothing to Him; it merely frustrates the power of the one who wields it.

46-47.word_for_word: अन्यद् अपि आश्चर्यम् आह — he describes another wonder; वत्स-पालाः — the calf-herd boys; वत्साः पालाश् च — both the calves and their keepers; सर्वे यष्टि-विषाणादयश् च — and all their sticks, horns and other belongings.
46-47.translation: He now describes another wonder: not only all the calves and all the calf-herd boys, but even every stick, horn and other possession associated with them manifested the same divine transformation.

48.word_for_word: श्रीवत्स-प्रभा-युक्तान् — endowed with the radiance of the Śrīvatsa mark; अङ्गदानि दोःषु — armlets upon their arms; रत्नमयानि कम्बु-वत् त्रि-धाराणि कङ्कणानि पाणिषु — jeweled bracelets on their wrists, three-ridged like a conch; ते च ते च — each and every one of them.
48.translation: Each form bore the radiant Śrīvatsa mark, armlets upon the arms, and jeweled bracelets on the wrists, marked with three ridges like a conch.

49.word_for_word: भूरि बहु-जन्म-अर्जितं पुण्यम् — abundant merit accumulated through many births; तद्-युक्तैः जनैः अर्पितैः — offered by people possessed of such merit.
49.translation: Their worship was offered by beings endowed with immense merit accumulated through many births.

50.word_for_word: चन्द्रिका-विशद-स्मित-युक्तैः — with smiles clear and bright as moonlight; सह-अरुण-गुणेन वर्तमाना अपाङ्गाः — sidelong glances also bearing a reddish hue; तैर् वीक्षितैः — by those glances; स्व-भक्त-मनोरथानाम् — of the wishes of their devotees; रजः-सत्त्वाभ्यां स्रष्टृ-पालका इव — as though creators through rajas and protectors through sattva; विशद-स्मितेन पालका इव — as protectors through the clear smile; अरुण-गुणेन स्रष्टार इव — as creators through the reddish quality.
50.translation: Their smiles were clear as moonlight and their sidelong glances tinged with red. By those looks they appeared to create and preserve the wishes of their devotees: the clear smile suggested the preserving quality of sattva, while the reddish glance suggested the creative quality of rajas.

51.word_for_word: आत्मा ब्रह्मा — Brahmā himself; तद्-आदि-स्तम्ब-पर्यन्तैः — from Brahmā down to the smallest immobile being; अनेकार्हैः — by innumerable worshipers; अनेकार्हणैः — with innumerable acts and objects of worship.
51.translation: From Brahmā himself down to the smallest stationary being, innumerable worshipers honored those forms with innumerable kinds of worship.

52.word_for_word: अजाद्याभिः — beginning with the unborn principle; माया-विद्यादिभिः — with māyā, vidyā and the rest; विभूतिभिः शक्तिभिः — with divine manifestations or powers; महद्-आदिभिः — beginning with mahat; महत्-सूत्रयोः पृथक्त्व-विवक्षया — when mahat and sūtra are counted separately; चतुर्-विंशति-तत्त्वैः — with the twenty-four principles; जगत्-कारणैः — causes of the universe.
52.translation: They were attended by divine powers beginning with māyā and vidyā and by the cosmic principles beginning with mahat. When mahat and sūtra are counted separately, these are the twenty-four causal principles of the universe.

53.word_for_word: कालादिभिः तत् सह-कारिभिः — with time and the other auxiliary causes; कालः क्षोभकः — time agitates primordial nature; स्वभावः परिणाम-हेतुः — inherent nature causes transformation; संस्कारः वासनाया उद्बोधकः — saṃskāra awakens latent tendencies; स्व-महि-ध्वस्त-महिभिः — whose own greatness was overwhelmed by a greater greatness; भगवन्-महिम्ना तिरस्कृत-स्वातन्त्र्यैः — whose independence was eclipsed by Bhagavān’s majesty; अणिमाद्यैः — by aṇimā and the other mystic powers.
53.translation: Time and the other auxiliary causes were also present: time produces agitation, inherent nature causes transformation, and saṃskāra awakens latent tendencies. The mystic powers beginning with aṇimā were there as well, but their own greatness and independence were completely eclipsed by Bhagavān’s majesty.

54.word_for_word: सर्वेषां मूर्तिमत्त्वे अपि विशेषम् आह — though all had visible forms, he states their unique nature; सत्याः ज्ञान-रूपाः अनन्ताः आनन्द-रूपाः — real, constituted of knowledge, infinite and constituted of bliss; तद्-एक-मात्राः — consisting solely of that; विजातीय-सम्भेद-रहिताः — free from admixture with anything of another kind; एक-रसाः सदैव एक-रूपाः — homogeneous and eternally of one nature; सत्य-ज्ञानादि-मात्रैक-रसं ब्रह्म तद् एव मूर्तिः येषाम् — alternatively, their very bodies were Brahman, whose sole essence is reality, knowledge and the rest; उपनिषद्-आत्म-ज्ञानं सैव दृक् चक्षुः येषाम् अपि — even for those whose eye is the Self-knowledge taught by the Upaniṣads; अस्पृष्ट-भूरि-माहात्म्याः — their immense glory remained beyond complete apprehension.
54.translation: Although all these manifestations had visible forms, their nature was unique: they were reality, knowledge, infinity and bliss itself, unmixed with anything of a different kind, homogeneous and eternally one in essence. Alternatively, their very bodies were Brahman, whose sole essence is reality, knowledge and bliss. Even those whose ‘eye’ is the knowledge of the Self taught by the Upaniṣads could not fully touch or comprehend their immense glory.

55.word_for_word: एवं सकृत् एकदा एव ददर्श — thus he saw it all at once, in a single moment; पर-ब्रह्मणः विशेषणं — the qualifying description belongs to the Supreme Brahman.
55.translation: Brahmā saw this entire manifestation all at once, in a single moment. The qualifying expressions in the verse describe the Supreme Brahman.

56.word_for_word: अति-कुतुकेन आश्चर्येण — from overwhelming astonishment; उद्वृत्य दृष्टीः परावृत्य — turning his eyes away, or rolling them back; हंस-पृष्ठे निपत्य — falling upon the back of his swan; पाठान्तरे उद्वृत्तः क्षुभितः — in another reading, ‘overwhelmed, agitated’; तेषां धाम्ना तेजसा स्तब्ध-सर्वेन्द्रियः — all his senses stunned by their radiance; ब्रह्मा तूष्णीं निश्चलः अभूत् — Brahmā became silent and motionless; पूर् देवी व्रजाधिष्ठात्री — the goddess presiding over Vraja; तस्या अन्ति पुत्रिका चतुर्-मुखी-कृतक-प्रतिमा इव — he looked like a little four-faced doll placed near that goddess.
56.translation: Overwhelmed by astonishment, Brahmā’s eyes rolled or turned away and he fell upon the back of his swan. Another reading describes him simply as violently agitated. The radiance of those forms stunned all his senses, leaving him silent and motionless, like a tiny four-faced doll placed beside the goddess who presides over Vraja.

57.word_for_word: मोह-मग्नम् अजम् उज्जहार — He drew the unborn Brahmā out of bewilderment; इरेशे — in Brahmā, lord of Irā/Sarasvatī; ‘किम् इदम्’ इति मुह्यति सति — while he wondered ‘what is this?’; तद् द्रष्टुम् अपि अनीशे — when he was no longer capable even of seeing it; परमोऽजः श्री-कृष्णः — the supreme unborn Śrī Kṛṣṇa; अजा-जवनिकां माया-रूपां तिरस्करिणीम् — the curtain of māyā associated with the unborn Brahmā; तां चच्छाद तिरो-धत्त अपसारितवान् — He covered/withdrew it, that is, removed the display; अथवा तस्योपरि मायां प्रसारितवान् — alternatively, He spread māyā over Brahmā, deeming him unfit to see His majesty; अतर्क्ये — in the inconceivable, beyond reasoning; निज-असाधारण-महिमनि — in His own unique majesty; स्व-प्रमितिके स्व-प्रकाशे सुखे — self-known, self-luminous bliss; अजातः प्रकृतेः परत्र — unborn, beyond prakṛti; अतन्-निरसन-मुखेन श्रुति-शिरोभिः मितिः — known by the Upaniṣads through negating what He is not.
57.translation: When Brahmā, lord of Sarasvatī, sank into bewilderment and could no longer even apprehend what he was seeing, the supreme unborn Śrī Kṛṣṇa brought him out of that state. Kṛṣṇa withdrew the curtain of māyā through which the astonishing display had appeared; alternatively, He spread māyā over Brahmā because that world-regent was unfit to continue beholding His majesty. Brahmā had been bewildered before Kṛṣṇa’s inconceivable and uniquely His own glory: the self-known, self-luminous bliss that is unborn and beyond prakṛti, known by the Upaniṣads through the method of negating everything that is not That.

58.word_for_word: अर्वाक् बहिः प्रतिलब्धानि अक्षीणि येन सः — one whose eyes again regained outward vision; परेतवत् मृतः यदि कथञ्चित् पुनः उत्तिष्ठति तथा — like a dead man who somehow rises again; दृष्टीः — eyes; नेत्राणि — the organs of sight.
58.translation: Brahmā regained the outward function of his eyes like a man thought dead who somehow rises again. ‘Dṛṣṭīḥ’ here simply means the eyes.

59.word_for_word: जनानाम् आजीव्यैः द्रुमैः आकीर्णम् — filled with trees that provide people’s livelihood; समा-प्रियम् — lovely in every respect; सन्ततानि आसमन्तात् प्रियाणि यस्मिन् — a place whose continuous surroundings were pleasant on every side.
59.translation: He saw Vṛndāvana filled with trees that sustain its inhabitants, continuously beautiful and delightful on every side.

60.word_for_word: नैसर्ग-दुर्वैराः — creatures naturally locked in irreconcilable enmity; नराः सिंहादयः च — animals such as men and lions/creatures such as lions and their prey; मित्राणि इव सह एव आसन् — lived together as though friends; अजितस्य आवासेन — because it was the abode of Ajita; द्रुताः पलायिताः रुट्-तर्षादयः — anger, greed and the like had fled away; तत्र अभूतं वृन्दावनम् अपश्यत् — he saw such extraordinary Vṛndāvana.
60.translation: In that extraordinary Vṛndāvana, creatures that are naturally irreconcilable enemies lived together like friends. Because it was the abode of Ajita, anger, greed and similar faults had fled from it. This was the Vṛndāvana Brahmā now saw.

61.word_for_word: परमेष्ठी ब्रह्मा पुरा पूर्ववत् एव ब्रह्म अचष्ट अपश्यत् — Brahmā again beheld Brahman as before; पशुप-वंश-शिशुत्वं नाट्यम् उद्वहत् — bearing the dramatic role of a child in a cowherd family; नाट्यम् इत्य् अत्र हेतुः अद्वयम् इत्यादि — ‘drama’ is justified by the descriptions ‘nondual’ and so forth; अद्वयं च वत्सान् विचिन्वत् — the nondual One searching for calves; एकं च सखीन् विचिन्वत् — the One searching for friends; अगाध-बोधं च विचिन्वत् — immeasurable consciousness appearing to seek; अनन्तं परितः विचिन्वत् — the Infinite searching all around; परं शिशुत्वम् उद्वहत् — the Supreme bearing childhood; ब्रह्म स-पाणि-कवलम् — Brahman with a morsel of food in His hand.
61.translation: Brahmā once again saw Brahman itself before him, now carrying on the dramatic role of a child in a cowherd family. It is rightly called a drama: the nondual One was searching for calves, the One for His friends; unfathomable consciousness seemed to be looking about, the Infinite searched in every direction, the Supreme bore the condition of childhood, and Brahman stood there with a morsel of food still in His hand.

62.word_for_word: निज-धोरणतः स्व-वाहनात् — from his own mount; त्वरेण वेगेन अवतीर्य — quickly descending; दण्डवत् नत्वा — prostrating like a staff; चतुर्णां मुकुटानाम् अग्रैः अङ्घ्रि-युग्मं स्पृष्ट्वा — touching Kṛṣṇa’s two feet with the tips of his four crowns; मुद्-अश्रु-सुजलैः — with pure tears of joy; अभिषेकम् अकरोत् — he performed an ablution.
62.translation: Brahmā swiftly descended from his own vehicle and fell flat like a staff. The tips of his four crowns touched Kṛṣṇa’s two feet, and with the pure water of his tears of joy he performed an ablution of those feet.

63.word_for_word: चिरस्य — for a long while; चिरं पादयोः पतन् आस्ते — he remained fallen at His feet for a long time.
63.translation: For a long while Brahmā remained fallen at Kṛṣṇa’s feet.

64.word_for_word: स-वेपथुः — trembling; स-कम्पः — shaking; अत एव गद्गदया — therefore with a choked voice; अनुकरणम् एतत् — this is an imitative/expressive verbal form; इलया वाचा — with speech; ऐलत — he praised; अस्तौत् — he offered hymns.
64.translation: Trembling all over, Brahmā’s voice became choked. With that faltering speech he began to praise and glorify Kṛṣṇa.
